components.note: 又 (hand) — traditionally a hand catching hold of a person from behind, hence "to reach"

example.pinyin: Qǐng jíshí huífù wǒ.
example.fact: 及 is a formal "and" in writing (A 及 B) and "to reach". It appears in 及时 (in time, promptly), 及格 (to pass an exam, literally "reach the standard"), 以及 (as well as) and 来不及 (not have enough time to).

components.note: 革 (leather) — shoes were traditionally made of leather
圭 (guī) gives only a loose, partial sound hint for xié

example.pinyin: Wǒ de xié tài xiǎo le.
example.fact: 鞋 counts with 双 (一双鞋), and one shoe is 只. You 穿鞋 (put on) and 脱鞋 (take off), and many types are named with it: 运动鞋 (sneakers), 拖鞋 (slippers), 皮鞋 (leather shoes).

components.note: 尸 (body) — a bodily function
比 (bǐ) gives a loose sound hint for pì

example.hanzi: 他放了一个屁，大家都笑了。
example.pinyin: Tā fàng le yí ge pì, dàjiā dōu xiào le.
example.fact: 屁 is blunt and informal: 放屁 is to fart and also to talk nonsense. 屁股 means buttocks, and 拍马屁 ("slap the horse's rump") means to flatter or suck up.

components.note: 目 (eye) — staring is done with the eyes
丁 (dīng) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Tā yìzhí dīng zhe wǒ kàn.
example.fact: 盯 means to stare or watch closely, usually with 着: 盯着. It also means to keep on top of something: 盯着孩子写作业 (watch over a child doing homework), and 盯梢 is to tail someone.

components.note: 土 (earth) — a heap of soil is the basic picture of piling
隹 (zhuī) gives a loose sound hint for duī

example.pinyin: Zhuōzi shang yǒu yì duī shū.
example.english: There's a pile of books on the table.
example.fact: 堆 is a measure word for piles of things: 一堆书, 一堆衣服. As a verb it means to pile up, as in 堆在一起; and 堆雪人 ("pile up a snowman") is the standard phrase for building a snowman.

components.note: 氵 (water) — deep water
罙 (shēn) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo hé hěn shēn.
example.fact: 深 is the opposite of 浅 (qiǎn). It extends from physical depth to depth of colour (深蓝 dark blue), time (深夜 late at night) and thought (深刻 profound).

components.note: 耳 (ear) — a traditional account links this to taking an ear as proof of a capture in ancient warfare
又 (hand) — the hand that takes

example.pinyin: Wǒ qù yínháng qǔ qián.
example.english: I'm going to the bank to withdraw money.
example.fact: 取 is to take or fetch: 取钱 (withdraw money), 取快递 (pick up a parcel), 取名 (choose a name), 取消 (cancel). It is more formal and specific than 拿 (to hold, take).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — biting is done with the mouth
交 (jiāo) gives a loose sound hint for yǎo

example.pinyin: Xiǎogǒu yǎo le wǒ yì kǒu.
example.fact: 咬 counts bites with 一口. It also appears in 咬牙 (clench teeth), 咬字 (to enunciate, as in 咬字清楚) and the idea of a tight fit or sticking to a point: 咬定 (insist firmly).

components.note: 矢 (arrow) — short arrows were used for measuring length
豆 (dòu) gives a loose sound hint for duǎn

example.pinyin: Zhè tiáo qúnzi tài duǎn le.
example.fact: 短 is the opposite of 长 and works for length and time: 短时间 (a short time). 短信 ("short message") is a text message, and 短视频 is a short video on apps like Douyin.

components.note: 糸 (silk thread) — pulling thread taut
又 (hand) — a hand drawing the thread tight

example.pinyin: Zhè shuāng xié yǒudiǎn jǐn.
example.english: These shoes are a bit tight.
example.fact: 紧 describes tight clothes or shoes (opposite 松), and the idea of tension: 紧张 (nervous), 紧急 (urgent), 抓紧 (to grab hold of, hurry up). 别紧张 is the everyday "don't be nervous".

components.note: 辶 (walk) — passing through something
秀 (xiù) gives a loose sound hint for tòu

example.pinyin: Yīfu dōu shī tòu le.
example.fact: 透 is often a result complement meaning "thoroughly": 湿透 (soaked), 看透 (see through), 想透 (think through). It also builds 透明 (transparent) and 透露 (to leak information).

components.note: A simple picture usually explained as a flexed arm or a digging tool, both suggesting physical effort

example.pinyin: Tā de lìqi hěn dà.
example.fact: 力 is the root of many words about ability or force: 力气 (physical strength), 努力 (effort), 能力 (ability), 压力 (pressure), 电力 (electric power). As a radical it appears in 动 and 办.

components.note: 刂 is the simplified left part, replacing the old left side of 帥
巾 (cloth) — recalls a commander's banner

example.pinyin: Tā zhǎng de hěn shuài.
example.fact: 帅 is the everyday word for "handsome" for men, while 帅哥 ("handsome guy") can be used to address any young man, like "sir". Its older meaning is commander: 元帅 (marshal), and the red general piece in Chinese chess is 帅.

components.note: 足 (foot) — kicking uses the foot
易 (yì) gives a loose sound hint for tī

example.pinyin: Tā xǐhuan tī zúqiú.
example.fact: 踢 is the verb for football: 踢足球, while basketball uses 打 (打篮球). It is also used for 踢毽子 (shuttlecock kicking) and in 踢被子, kicking off the bedcovers while asleep.

components.note: 日 (sun) — stars are points of light like small suns
生 (shēng) gives the sound — they share the same vowel

example.pinyin: Jīnwǎn tiānshang yǒu hěn duō xīngxing.
example.english: There are lots of stars in the sky tonight.
example.fact: 星 appears in 星期 (week) and its days (星期一…), in 明星 (celebrity, "bright star"), and in hotel ratings: 五星级. The stars themselves are counted with 颗: 一颗星.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pushing uses the hand
隹 (zhuī) gives the sound — they share the same final

example.pinyin: Qǐng tuī yíxià mén.
example.fact: 推 is the opposite of 拉 (lā), the pair printed on shop doors. It also means to recommend (推荐), postpone (推迟), refuse (推辞) and deduce (推理).

components.note: 斤 (axe) — cutting something through
The left part is the simplified remnant of bundled silk threads being cut

example.pinyin: Shǒujī xìnhào tūrán duàn le.
example.english: The phone signal suddenly cut out.
example.fact: 断 is for things that break in two or are cut off, such as ropes, lines and connections: 断电 (power cut), 绳子断了 (the rope snapped), 不断 (continuously, "not breaking"), 判断 (to judge).

components.note: 穴 (cave) — a hollow space
工 (gōng) gives the sound — they share the same final

example.pinyin: Píngzi shì kōng de.
example.fact: 空 has two readings: kōng (empty, sky: 空气, 天空, 空调) and kòng (free time or empty space: 有空, 空位). "你有空吗?" (Are you free?) therefore uses kòng.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — holding is a hand-and-arm action
包 (bāo) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.pinyin: Māma bàozhe háizi.
example.fact: 抱 is to hold something in the arms, and 拥抱 is a hug. It extends to emotions: 抱歉 (sorry, "hold regret"), 抱怨 (complain) and 抱希望 (hold hope).

components.note: 王 (here the old jade 玉, twice) — pieces of jade
刂 (knife) — cutting jade in two, i.e. dividing, which suggests dividing people into groups

example.pinyin: Wǒmen bān yǒu èrshí gè xuésheng.
example.english: There are twenty students in our class.
example.fact: 班 is a class or group (我们班, 班长), and also a work shift: 上班 (go to work), 下班 (get off work), 加班 (work overtime). It counts scheduled services too: 航班 (flight), 班车 (shuttle bus).

meanings: measure word for planes and pianos

components.note: 木 (wood) — frames and racks were built of wood
加 (jiā) gives the sound — they differ only in tone

example.pinyin: Shūjià shang yǒu hěn duō shū.
example.english: There are many books on the bookshelf.
example.fact: 架 is a frame or rack (书架 bookshelf) and a measure word for machines and instruments such as planes and pianos: 一架飞机, 一架钢琴. 吵架 and 打架 (quarrel, fight) use it too, and 摆架子 means to put on airs.

components.note: Simplified form of 聖; the new top 又 and bottom 土 no longer show the old ear-and-mouth picture

example.pinyin: Shèngdàn Jié kuàilè!
example.fact: 圣 means holy or sage: 圣人 (sage), 神圣 (sacred), 圣经 (the Bible). 圣诞节 is Christmas, literally "holy birth festival", and 圣诞老人 is Santa Claus.

components.note: 冫 (ice, still water) — still water is a level and so a standard
隹 (zhuī) gives only a loose sound hint for zhǔn

example.pinyin: Tā de fāyīn hěn zhǔn.
example.fact: 准 means accurate (准确) and to allow (不准 "not permitted" is stricter than 不可以). It is also in the everyday 准备 (to prepare) and 准时 (punctual), and as a prefix "quasi", e.g. 准妈妈 (mother-to-be).

components.note: 扌 (hand) — snatching is a hand action
仓 (cāng) gives a loose sound hint for qiǎng

example.pinyin: Xiǎotōu qiǎng zǒu le tā de bāo.
example.english: The thief snatched her bag away.
example.fact: 抢 is to snatch or rob, and in daily life to rush to get something: 抢票 (grab tickets, a New Year ritual), 抢红包 (grab WeChat red envelopes), 抢购 (panic-buy) and 抢救 (to rescue in an emergency).

components.note: 讠 (speech) — lessons are taught by speaking
果 (guǒ) gives a loose sound hint for kè

example.hanzi: 今天下午我们有两节课。
example.pinyin: Jīntiān xiàwǔ wǒmen yǒu liǎng jié kè.
example.english: We have two classes this afternoon.
example.fact: 课 counts class periods with 节: 一节课. You 上课 (go to class), 下课 (class ends), and talk about 课本 (textbook) and 课程 (course). Homework is 作业, not 课.

components.note: 身 (body) — lying down is a body posture
尚 (shàng) gives the sound — they share the same final

example.pinyin: Tā tǎng zài chuáng shang kàn shū.
example.fact: 躺 is to lie on your back or side, while 趴 (pā) is to lie face down. 躺平 ("lie flat") became popular internet slang around 2021 for opting out of the rat race.

components.note: A picture of a mountain with several peaks

example.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen qù pá shān.
example.fact: 山 counts with 座 (一座山). 爬山 is hiking, 山水 ("mountains and water") means landscape, especially in painting, and 山 is the radical in many mountain-related characters such as 岛 and 峰.

components.note: 止 (foot, stop) is the upper part
⺼ (flesh) — traditionally traced to a piece of meat on a bone, later borrowed for "willing"

example.pinyin: Tā bù kěn gàosu wǒ.
example.fact: 肯 means to be willing and is most often negated: 不肯 means to refuse. It also builds 肯定 (certain, to affirm) and the pattern 肯 + verb: 他肯帮忙 (he is willing to help).

components.note: 疒 (sickness) — pain is a bodily ailment
甬 (yǒng) gives a loose sound hint for tòng

example.pinyin: Wǒ dùzi hěn tòng.
example.fact: 痛 is a bit more formal than 疼 (téng) and often sharper or more emotional: 痛苦 (suffering), 痛恨 (hate bitterly), 痛哭 (weep bitterly). 痛快 ("pain-fast") oddly means happy and unrestrained.

components.note: Simplified form of 親; the modern shape no longer shows the old parts, but the word stays tied to closeness

example.pinyin: Tā hé wǒ shì qīn xiōngdì.
example.english: He and I are brothers by blood.
example.fact: 亲 is closeness of blood or feeling: 父亲, 母亲, 亲戚 (relatives), 亲爱的 (dear). As a verb it is the casual "kiss" (亲一下), and Chinese online sellers address customers as 亲, like "dear".

components.note: Traditionally a hand peeling a hide off an animal

example.pinyin: Zhège píngguǒ de pí hěn báo.
example.english: This apple's skin is very thin.
example.fact: 皮 covers skin, peel and leather: 皮肤 (skin), 皮鞋 (leather shoes), 苹果皮 (apple peel). Used as an adjective it also means naughty: 这孩子很皮, "that kid is mischievous".

components.note: A picture of a bird seen from the side, with head, body and tail

example.pinyin: Shù shang yǒu yì zhī niǎo.
example.english: There is a bird in the tree.
example.fact: 鸟 counts with 只 (一只鸟) and is the radical in many bird names, such as 鸡 and 鸭. The slang reading diǎo is crude, so learners should stick to niǎo for the animal.

components.note: 大 (a person with arms spread) stands in the middle
爻 (crossing marks, written twice) on either side — a traditional picture of light shining through

example.pinyin: Xǐ wán zǎo, gǎnjué zhēn shuǎng.
example.english: I feel so refreshed after the bath.
example.fact: 爽 means refreshing or satisfying, as in 凉爽 (cool and crisp) and the slang 爽! for "that feels great". It also means straightforward (爽快) and, surprisingly, to break a promise: 爽约 means to stand someone up.

components.note: 囗 (enclosure) — a closed loop
卷 (juǎn) gives a loose sound hint for quān

example.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèngquè dá'àn shang huà quān.
example.fact: 圈 is a circle or ring and counts laps: 跑一圈 (run one lap). It also means social circle, which is why WeChat Moments is called 朋友圈, "circle of friends".

components.note: 口 (mouth) — a breathy sound made with the mouth
虚 (xū) gives the sound — an exact match

example.pinyin: Xū, xiǎoshēng diǎn, bǎobao shuì zháo le.
example.english: Shh, be quiet, the baby is asleep.
example.fact: 嘘 is the "shh!" sound for hushing, and it also means to hiss or boo (嘘声). The idiom 嘘寒问暖 ("puff warmth, ask about the cold") describes caring attentively for someone's well-being.

components.note: 木 (tree) — a tree
对 (duì) stands in for the old phonetic 尌 (shù), so the sound match is loose

example.pinyin: Yuànzi lǐ yǒu yì kē dà shù.
example.english: There's a big tree in the yard.
example.fact: 树 counts with 棵 (一棵树). As a verb it means to establish: 树立. The proverb 十年树木，百年树人 (ten years to grow a tree, a hundred to cultivate people) is the classic line about education.

components.note: 页 (head) — the neck is part of the head and body
工 (gōng) gives only a loose sound hint for xiàng

example.pinyin: Zhège xiàngmù yǒu sān xiàng rènwu.
example.fact: 项 is a measure word for items, tasks and events: 一项任务, 一项比赛. It builds 项目 (project) and 项链 (necklace, literally "neck chain"), keeping its original sense of neck.

components.note: 贝 (shell, old money) — the radical for value; its link to contests is faint

example.pinyin: Míngtiān yǒu yì chǎng zúqiú sài.
example.english: There is a football match tomorrow.
example.fact: 赛 is a contest, counted with 场: 一场比赛. It forms 比赛 (match), 决赛 (final), 赛跑 (race) and 赛车 (racing car). Note that it is a bound word rather than a free noun.

components.note: 亻 (person) — passing something along between people
专 (zhuān) gives the sound — they share the same final

example.hanzi: 请把这个消息传给大家。
example.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zhège xiāoxi chuán gěi dàjiā.
example.english: Please pass this news on to everyone.
example.fact: 传 is to pass on, as in 传染 (infect), 传说 (legend) and 传统 (tradition). Read zhuàn, the same character means a biography (自传, 传记): a classic two-reading trap.

components.note: Water flowing around small islets; 州 originally meant an islet, later an administrative area

example.pinyin: Wǒ qù guo Guǎngzhōu.
example.fact: 州 was an ancient administrative division and survives in city names (广州, 杭州, 苏州) and in the names of U.S. states (加州 California). The meaning "islet" was later split into its own character 洲, which now means continent (亚洲).

components.note: 口 (mouth) — noise made with the mouth
少 (shǎo) gives the sound — they share the same final

example.pinyin: Wàimiàn tài chǎo le, wǒ shuì bù zháo.
example.english: It's too noisy outside, I can't sleep.
example.fact: 吵 is noisy as an adjective and to quarrel as a verb: 吵架 (argue). 吵醒 means to wake someone with noise, and 别吵 means "don't make noise". It is milder than 闹 (nào), which suggests more commotion.

components.note: 禾 (grain) — harvest, wealth
刂 (knife) — cutting grain, and so also sharpness

example.pinyin: Zhè duì nǐ yǒulì.
example.fact: 利 means advantage and sharp, and so also profit: 利息 (interest), 利润 (profit). 顺利 (smooth) and 胜利 (victory) are staples, and 利弊 ("advantage and drawback") means pros and cons.

components.note: 片 (a flat slice, originally a piece of wood) — flat tablets and cards
卑 (bēi) gives only a loose sound hint for pái

example.pinyin: Tāmen zài dǎ pái.
example.fact: 牌 is a card, tile or sign: 打牌 (play cards or mahjong), 扑克牌 (playing cards), 招牌 (shop sign), 门牌 (house number plate). As a brand it appears in 品牌 and 名牌 (famous brand).

components.note: Two strokes splitting apart; the original sense is "to divide", borrowed for the number eight

example.pinyin: Wǒ bā diǎn qǐchuáng.
example.english: I get up at eight o'clock.
example.fact: 八 is a lucky number because it sounds like 发 (fā, "to prosper"). The Beijing Olympics opened on 8 August 2008 at 8:08 pm for this reason. Phone numbers and car plates with 8s sell at a premium.

components.note: A picture of a tuft of hair or fur

example.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo de máo hěn ruǎn.
example.english: This cat's fur is very soft.
example.fact: 毛 is body hair and fur. In money, colloquially, 毛 is one tenth of a yuan: 五毛 is fifty fen (the written form is 角). It also means rough or crude: 毛病 (a fault), and Mao is a common surname.

components.note: 士 (scholar, man) — a person of standing
口 (mouth) — speaking good words

example.pinyin: Zhù nǐ jíxiáng rúyì.
example.english: I wish you good fortune and all you desire.
example.fact: 吉 means lucky, as in 吉利 and 吉祥. Chinese people choose a 吉日 (auspicious day) for weddings and openings. It is also used for sound in transliterations such as 吉他 (guitar).

components.note: 心 (heart) — stirring up feelings
若 (ruò) gives a loose sound hint for rě

example.pinyin: Bié rě tā, tā píqi bù hǎo.
example.english: Don't provoke him, he has a bad temper.
example.fact: 惹 is to provoke or cause: 惹麻烦 (cause trouble), 惹事 (stir up trouble), 惹不起 (can't afford to offend). Interestingly 惹人喜欢 means "lovable", as it attracts people's affection.

components.note: 扌 (hand) — pulling something out by hand
由 (yóu) gives a loose sound hint for chōu

example.pinyin: Tā bù chōu yān.
example.fact: 抽 is to pull something out: 抽烟 (smoke, literally "draw smoke"), 抽奖 (draw a prize), 抽血 (draw blood), 抽屉 (drawer) and 抽空 (to squeeze out some time).

components.note: Traditionally explained as three horizontals for heaven, humans and earth joined by a vertical stroke, the king who connects them

example.pinyin: Shīzi shì sēnlín zhī wáng.
example.english: The lion is the king of the forest.
example.fact: 王 is a king, and 王 is also one of the most common Chinese surnames. It can mean the top of a kind: 歌王 (king of song), and the radical 王 also appears in jade-related characters, where it is a form of 玉.

components.note: 巾 (cloth) — the original sense was a long garment, extended to "constant"
尚 (shàng) gives a loose sound hint for cháng

example.pinyin: Wǒ chángcháng qù nà jiā kāfēidiàn.
example.english: I often go to that coffee shop.
example.fact: 常 means usual and often: 常常 (often), 经常 (frequently), 平常 (ordinary), 正常 (normal), 日常 (everyday). Both 常常 and 经常 are common, with 常 alone slightly more concise.
